meta.title: More in Common polling for 11 London — June 2023
meta.form_intro: A short survey about health, the NHS, charities and how people in Britain get on. There are no right or wrong answers; answer as yourself.
notes: Q7 was a split sample in the real survey: half were asked about 'support', half about 'advice' (weighted N about 1,015 / 1,003). The simulated form asks every agent both; each is scored against its own half.
Q12 was asked only of those who said Yes at Q11 (weighted N 507); the simulated base is routed the same way.
Q14 and Q18 are open text: kept as verbatims for qualitative comparison, not scored.
Long-term condition (Q5) is a survey answer and a banner column in the workbook; it is never used to build agents.

questions.text: Which of the following health issues should be the biggest priority for the government? Select up to three
And of those you chose in question 1, which should be the biggest priority for the government? Select only one
Generally speaking, do you think that each of the following issues is talked about too much, too little or about the right amount?
How much trust do you have in the following?
Do you have an existing long-term health condition?
What feature would most encourage you to use a health app on your smartphone or smart watch? Select one
How much trust do you have in the following to give you support with your health?
How much trust do you have in the following to give you advice with your health?
How familiar are you with the term 'clinical trials'?
Regarding clinical trials, please select the statements you most agree with (up to three)
Do you think people with the following conditions should be receiving free treatment on the NHS?
Have you ever not taken medications that you were advised to take?
Why was that? Select all that apply

Which do you agree with most?
Do you agree or disagree with the following statements?
